newsitem.title: JAPAN: JR West to cut workforce by 25 pct in next decade.
newsitem.headline: JR West to cut workforce by 25 pct in next decade.

text.p: West Japan Railway Co (JR West) said on Wednesday that it plans to cut its workforce of 47,000 by more than 25 percent in the next 10 years.

"We expect that a total of 20,000 staff will retire or leave the company in the next 10 years. Taking new hiring into consideration, the total number of workers will decline by 12,000," JR West executive director Hiroaki Takahashi told a news conference at which the company's interim earnings were announced.
JR West, which operates railway services in western Japan, announced that its current profits for the first half of the 1996/97 business year increased 8.6 percent to 37.939 billion yen.
However, the company's half-year operating profit was down slightly, partly due to payments for its early retirement programme, a company official said.
Former Japan National Railways was split into seven Japan Railway group companies in April 1987. West Japan Railway is one the spin offs.
The company listed its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and Osaka Securities Exchange on October 8, 1995.
